Nuclei of the brainstem

The nuclei of the brainstem are gray matter masses embedded in its substance. They are divided into tract nuclei and cranial nerve nuclei.

Tract nuclei

These are stations in the course of the tracts ascending to and descending from the brainstem.

Medulla oblongata
Gracile and cuneate nuclei
Pons
Pontine nuclei
Midbrain
Red nucleus; nuclei of the superior and inferior colliculi

Cranial nerve nuclei

Definition

Cranial nerve nuclei send motor fibers to, or receive sensory fibers from, the cranial nerves.

Components of cranial nerve fibers

In shortCranial nerve fibers have 7 possible components: 3 motor and 4 sensory.

Cranial nerve fiber components
  • Motor (3)
    • General somatic efferent (GSE) voluntary muscles from myotomes
    • General visceral efferent (GVE) involuntary muscles and glands
    • Special visceral efferent (SVE) branchial arch muscles
  • Sensory (4)
    • General somatic afferent (GSA) cutaneous sensation and proprioception
    • Special somatic afferent (SSA) hearing and equilibrium
    • General visceral afferent (GVA) visceral distension and chemical conditions
    • Special visceral afferent (SVA) taste and smell

The general somatic afferent component receives cutaneous sensation (pain, temperature, touch, vibration or pressure) and proprioceptive sensation from muscles, joints, ligaments and periosteum.

Don't confuse

Unlike cranial nerves, spinal nerves contain only 4 fiber components: general somatic and visceral afferent, and general somatic and visceral efferent.

Position and arrangement of the nuclei

The position of the nuclei differs according to the position of the gray matter in the brainstem.

Lower (closed) medulla and midbrain

  • Nuclei lie in relation to the central canal and the cerebral aqueduct

Upper (open) medulla and pons

  • Nuclei lie in relation to the floor of the 4th ventricle

The nuclei are arranged in columns within the brainstem according to the cranial nerve components. The nuclei of each column are concerned with the same component.

Motor columns

General somatic efferent column

Concerned with the supply of the extraocular and tongue muscles. It includes the nuclei of nerves III, IV, VI and XII.

NucleusSiteStructures supplied
Oculomotor nerve IIIUpper midbrainAll extraocular muscles except lateral rectus and superior oblique

General visceral efferent column

Supplies the intraocular muscles, digestive and respiratory viscera, the heart and glands.

NucleusSiteStructures supplied
Edinger Westphal nucleusUpper midbrainIntraocular muscles: ciliary and constrictor pupillae
Superior salivary nucleusPonsSublingual, submandibular and lacrimal glands
Inferior salivary nucleusMedullaParotid glands
Dorsal nucleus of vagusMedullaStimulatory to digestive and respiratory viscera; inhibitory to the heart

Special visceral efferent column

Supplies muscles derived from the branchial arches, for example facial, mastication, pharyngeal and laryngeal muscles.

High-yield

Unlike true striated muscles, branchial muscles are not completely under voluntary control.

NucleusSiteStructures supplied
Trigeminal nerve V motor nucleusPonsMuscles of mastication, tensor palati, tensor tympani, anterior belly of digastric, mylohyoid
Facial nerve VII motor nucleusLower ponsFacial muscles, posterior belly of digastric, stylohyoid
Nucleus ambiguusMedullaPharyngeal and laryngeal muscles

Sensory columns

High-yield

The general somatic afferent column is the only uninterrupted column in the brainstem.

ColumnNucleusSiteSensation received
Special visceral afferentSolitary nucleusMedullaTaste, through fibers of trigeminal V, facial VII and vagus X nerves
General visceral afferentCommissural nucleus (most caudal part of the solitary nucleus)Midline of closed medullaVisceral sensation from digestive and respiratory systems, carotid sinus and body, aortic arch
General somatic afferentMesencephalic nucleusMidbrainProprioception from the face
General somatic afferentMain sensory nucleusPonsDiscriminative touch and pressure from the face
General somatic afferentSpinal nucleus of trigeminal nerve VMedullaPain and temperature from the face, pharynx and larynx
Special somatic afferentDorsal and ventral cochlear nucleiPontomedullary junctionHearing
Special somatic afferent4 vestibular nuclei (superior, inferior, medial and lateral)Pontomedullary junctionEquilibrium

The general somatic afferent column is concerned with sensation from the face through the trigeminal nerve V, and from the pharynx and larynx through the glossopharyngeal IX and vagus X nerves. The special somatic afferent column receives hearing and equilibrium through the vestibulocochlear nerve VIII.

Check yourself

Which nucleus in the pons supplies the lateral rectus?

The abducent nerve VI nucleus.

Which nucleus supplies the pharyngeal and laryngeal muscles, and where is it?

The nucleus ambiguus, in the medulla (special visceral efferent column).

Which brainstem sensory column is the only uninterrupted one?

The general somatic afferent column.

Key Points / Quick Review

Types of brainstem nuclei

  • Tract nuclei: gracile and cuneate (medulla), pontine nuclei (pons), red nucleus and colliculi nuclei (midbrain)
  • Cranial nerve nuclei: send motor fibers to or receive sensory fibers from cranial nerves

Components

  • Cranial nerves: 7 components (3 motor: GSE, GVE, SVE; 4 sensory: GSA, SSA, GVA, SVA)
  • Spinal nerves: only 4 components

Position

  • Closed medulla and midbrain: around central canal and cerebral aqueduct
  • Open medulla and pons: related to the floor of the 4th ventricle

Motor nuclei

  • GSE: III (upper midbrain), IV (lower midbrain), VI (pons), XII (medulla)
  • GVE: Edinger Westphal, superior salivary, inferior salivary, dorsal nucleus of vagus
  • SVE: trigeminal motor (pons), facial motor (lower pons), nucleus ambiguus (medulla)

Sensory nuclei

  • SVA: solitary nucleus (taste); GVA: commissural nucleus
  • GSA: mesencephalic, main sensory, spinal nucleus of V (the only uninterrupted column)
  • SSA: cochlear and vestibular nuclei at the pontomedullary junction
